chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-Ala' from Muhammad from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He was asked about a man who joined the Imam in his prayer, having previously performed one rak'ah ahead of him. When the Imam finished, he left with the people, then remembered afterwards that one rak'ah had been missed by him. He said: 'He repeats it as one single rak'ah.'

key_terms.سَبَقَهُ بِرَكْعَةٍ: he preceded him by one rak'ah
key_terms.فَاتَتْهُ: missed him / was missed by him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who joins the Imam late and realizes they missed a rak'ah after the prayer ends?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of simplicity in correcting congregational prayer errors, specifically addressing the scenario where a latecomer realizes a missed rak'ah after the Imam has concluded. It highlights the distinction between the worshipper's independent action and their subsequent integration into the congregation, emphasizing that the obligation is limited to completing the deficit rather than restarting. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on practical ease (*rukhas*) in ritual worship, ensuring that minor oversights do not burden the faithful with excessive re-performance.
